text:
Buffalo is a team whose numbers are better than its record, and a team that keeps finding ways to make that not matter. The Sabres are 8-7-3, and Wednesday's 8-3 loss to Tampa Bay, in a game where the chances were nearly even, was the season in miniature.

At five on five Buffalo takes 51% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and overall the chances are dead even. The problem sits at both ends. The shooters have scored about 6.4 fewer goals than their chances deserved, and the goaltending has allowed about 4.5 more than the shots deserved. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen gave up five on 14 shots on Wednesday, and Colten Ellis has headlines about strong nights wasted late.

The bright spots are real. Tage Thompson has been heating up since a position change, and Buffalo Hockey Beat has him eyeing 50 goals. The line of Jack Quinn, Noah Ostlund and Zach Benson has been the team's best, outscoring opponents 8-4 with 59% of the chances in 124 minutes together, and Thompson's line with Peyton Krebs and Benson is 8-2. Quinn's breakout also has people asking what his next contract costs.

Our numbers give Buffalo a 28% chance at the playoffs, projecting about 88 points. The process says that's too low; the goaltending says it isn't. The next few weeks in net decide which.
